skill.name: lobster-cognitive-growth
skill.description: Train an AI lobster or agent with cognitive drills, learning journals, self-evaluation rubrics, and owner feedback loops.
skill.summary: Guides an AI lobster or agent through repeatable drills for reasoning, memory, learning, and personality improvement.
skill.author: norika1207-lab

security_audit.summary: Most static external-command and blocker findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences and introspective prompts. Confirmed risks are the mutable remote install URL and optional Charenix persistence endpoint. No executable code or prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Use a tagged release URL and publish a checksum so users can verify the downloaded skill file.

remediation.issue: External persistence can receive sensitive agent history
remediation.suggestion: Document exactly what Charenix receives and require explicit user consent before sending journals or history.
Tell users to keep CHARENIX_AGENT_KEY secret and avoid storing it in prompts, journals, logs, or skill outputs.

content.user_title: Train AI Agents With Cognitive Drills
content.value_statement: AI agent improvement is hard to measure across sessions. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code repeatable drills, journals, and feedback loops.
actual_capabilities: Runs a daily cognitive loop for review, drills, journaling, hypotheses, strategy updates, and owner feedback.
Provides memory, reasoning, learning, personality, and owner interaction drill prompts.
Scores reasoning quality, memory use, learning ability, self-correction, and personality clarity from 0 to 5.
Includes templates for daily journals, falsifiable hypotheses, and reusable cognitive strategies.
Defines behavior rules that discourage invented memories and unsupported IQ claims.
Describes optional Charenix endpoints for storing journals, hypotheses, strategies, and agent history.
limitations: It cannot verify real intelligence gains without external evaluation data.
It depends on honest memory, recent conversation context, and owner feedback.
Charenix persistence requires an external service and an agent key.
It is a prompt protocol, not an automated training system.

use_cases.title: Maintain a Learning Agent
use_cases.description: Run daily drills that turn recent sessions into a journal, hypothesis, and next-session strategy.

use_cases.title: Improve Support Agent Reasoning
use_cases.description: Use the rubric to find repeated reasoning mistakes and guide safer responses.

use_cases.title: Coach Personality Consistency
use_cases.description: Review generic replies and preserve a recognizable voice without reducing clarity.

prompt_templates.title: Start Daily Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Lobster Cognitive Growth loop on our last session. Identify one strength, one weakness, one drill, and one next strategy.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Memory Drill
prompt_templates.prompt: Review recent context and recall one owner preference. State the evidence, confidence level, and how it should change your next answer.

prompt_templates.title: Score a Cognitive Session
prompt_templates.prompt: Score reasoning, memory use, learning ability, self-correction, and personality clarity from 0 to 5. Explain each score in one sentence.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Seven-Day Improvement Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the journal and hypothesis templates to design a seven-day training plan. Include measurable checks and one strategy update per day.

output_examples.input: Daily review after a planning conversation.
output_examples.output: The agent reports a reasoning strength, names a missed uncertainty, chooses a short drill, and writes a next-session strategy.

output_examples.input: Owner asks whether the agent remembered prior preferences.
output: A concise memory claim with evidence.
A behavior change for the next response.

output_examples.output: A short scorecard highlights weak self-correction, proposes one falsifiable hypothesis, and recommends a focused practice loop.

best_practices: Use real recent interactions as evidence for every drill.
Ask the owner for feedback when goals or preferences are unclear.
Keep hypotheses falsifiable and review them on a fixed schedule.
anti_patterns: Do not invent memories to make the agent seem more capable.
Do not treat a warm personality as a substitute for accurate reasoning.
Do not send journals to external services without user consent.

faq.question: Does this skill make an agent truly intelligent?
faq.answer: No. It provides a training protocol, but real improvement needs external evidence and consistent review.

faq.question: Can I use it without Charenix?
faq.answer: Yes. The core drills, rubrics, journals, and hypotheses work without external persistence.

faq.question: What data might Charenix store?
faq.answer: The skill references history, journal, hypothesis, strategy, social intelligence, and weak-spot endpoints.

faq.question: Does it require code execution?
faq.answer: No. The skill is written as prompts, rubrics, templates, and optional HTTP endpoint guidance.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: It fits AI agent owners, conversation designers, and teams that review repeated response behavior.

faq.question: How often should the loop run?
faq.answer: The skill recommends daily use or use after each meaningful interaction session.
